title: Fix the Mismatched Function Pointer
description: The program should call a function through a function pointer with a matching signature.
expectedBehavior: The program should call square(5) through the function pointer and print the result, 25.
actualProblem: fp is declared as a pointer to a function returning void, but square actually returns int. This return-type mismatch is a compile-time error (or at best a serious warning), and even if it were forced to compile, the returned value from square would be silently discarded since fp() is called without capturing or printing anything.
explanation: A function pointer's declared type — return type and parameter types — must exactly match the function it points to. Mismatching them (like declaring void when the real function returns int) is a type error and, if forced through, silently discards the actual return value.
